questions.stem: Which formula is equivalent to ¬(p ∨ q)?
questions.explain: De Morgan: negating an OR turns it into an AND of the negations.
The loops try all four (p, q) pairs. (not p) or q is false only for p = True, q = False, so three pairs count.

questions.stem: Which formula is equivalent to p → q?
questions.explain: p → q is false only when p is true and q is false, which is exactly when ¬p ∨ q is false.

questions.stem: What is the contrapositive of p → q?
questions.explain: The contrapositive swaps and negates both sides, and it is always equivalent to the original. ¬p → ¬q is the inverse and q → p is the converse; they are not equivalent.

questions.stem: ¬∀x P(x) is equivalent to which statement?
questions.explain: Saying "P holds for every x" fails exactly when some x makes P false: ∃x ¬P(x).
